units.grammar: Question forms. Yes/No questions in simple tenses need do, does or did + infinitive: Does Marta cycle to school? Did you lock the door? With be, continuous and perfect tenses and modal verbs, put the auxiliary before the subject: Is he ready? Have they left? Can you swim? Wh- questions use the same order after the question word: Where does your cousin live? Why were you laughing?
existing_questions_sample: ____ your sister play the guitar? (Do / Does / Is) | Does
Where ____ you go last weekend? (do / did / were) | did
Correct it: Who did phone you last night? | Who phoned you last night?
____ they watching TV when you arrived? (Did / Were / Have) | Were
Put in order: long / how / you / have / here / lived | How long have you lived here?
What time ____ the film start tonight? (do / does / is) | does
Correct it: What means this word? | What does this word mean?
Who ____ (live) in that old house? Mr Grant does. | lives
____ you ever eaten sushi? (Did / Have / Are) | Have
Correct it: Why you are late? | Why are you late?
Make a question: She can speak Italian. ____ Italian? | Can she speak
What ____ (happen) at the party last night? | happened

units.grammar: Present tense review. Present simple for habits, routines, permanent situations and facts: My dad works in a bank. Water freezes at 0 degrees. Present continuous for things happening now, temporary situations and fixed future plans: I'm staying with my aunt this week. We're meeting Sam at six.
existing_questions_sample: My brother usually ____ (get) up at seven. | gets
Be quiet! The baby ____ (sleep). | is sleeping
Correct it: I'm not understanding this exercise. | I don't understand this exercise.
We've lived in this flat ____ 2020. (for / since) | since
She ____ (know) my cousin for ten years. | has known
I ____ (meet) Dani at the cinema tonight. It's all arranged. | am meeting
They've been friends ____ a long time. (for / since) | for
Correct it: This soup is tasting delicious. | This soup tastes delicious.
Water ____ (boil) at 100 degrees. | boils
Why ____ (you / wear) a coat? It's hot today! | are you wearing
I ____ him since last summer. (know / am knowing / have known) | have known
Sara ____ (stay) with her gran this week because her parents are away. | is staying

units.grammar: Past tense review. Past simple for finished actions and past states: We moved here in 2019. I didn't like vegetables as a child. Past continuous (was/were + -ing) for an action in progress at a past moment, or as background: At nine I was walking the dog. A longer action (past continuous) is often interrupted by a shorter one (past simple): I was having a shower when the phone rang.
existing_questions_sample: I ____ (watch) a series when the lights went out. | was watching
When I got to the station, the train ____ (already / leave). | had already left
We ____ (go) to Portugal last summer. | went
My mum ____ to have long hair, but now it's short. (use / used) | used
Correct it: Did you used to play football? | Did you use to play football?
While they ____ (walk) home, it started to rain. | were walking
She was tired because she ____ (not / sleep) well the night before. | hadn't slept
Correct it: I was breaking my arm last year. | I broke my arm last year.
I didn't ____ to like coffee. (use / used) | use
What ____ (you / do) at eight o'clock last night? | were you doing
He ____ (drop) his phone while he was running for the bus. | dropped
By the time we arrived, everyone ____ (go) home. | had gone

units.grammar: Making comparisons. Use comparative + than, or less + adjective + than: Trains are faster than buses. This phone is less expensive than that one. as + adjective + as means equal; not as/so ... as means less: Leo is as tall as his dad. My room isn't as big as yours. the + comparative, the + comparative shows that two things change together: The more you practise, the better you play.
existing_questions_sample: My bike is ____ (cheap) than yours. | cheaper
This exam wasn't as hard ____ the last one. (as / than / that) | as
The ____ (early) we leave, the sooner we'll arrive. | earlier
Correct it: She is more tall than her brother. | She is taller than her brother.
Madrid is ____ bigger than Toledo. (far / very / by far) | far
It's by ____ the funniest film I've seen. (far / much / lot) | far
The book is ____ (good) than the film. | better
Correct it: He isn't as fast than me. | He isn't as fast as me.
Today is a ____ colder than yesterday. (bit / very / more) | bit
The more I study, the ____ (little) I worry. | less
Cycling is ____ dangerous than skiing. (less / least / fewer) | less
That was ____ the worst meal ever. (easily / far / very) | easily

units.grammar: Relative clauses. Defining relative clauses say which person or thing we mean, with no commas: The girl who sits next to me is from Peru. Use who/that for people, which/that for things, whose for possession, where for places and when for times. You can leave out who, which or that when it is the object of the clause: The film (that) we saw was brilliant. But not when it is the subject: The boy who won is my cousin.
existing_questions_sample: That's the boy ____ dog bit me. (who / whose / which) | whose
This is the café ____ we had breakfast. (which / where / when) | where
My aunt, ____ lives in Chile, is visiting us. (that / who / which) | who
Correct it: Rome, that is huge, is amazing. | Rome, which is huge, is amazing.
Can we leave out 'that'? The song that I love is on. (yes / no) | yes
Can we leave out 'who'? The man who called was rude. (yes / no) | no
I'll never forget the day ____ we met. (when / where / whose) | when
The laptop ____ I use for school is very slow. (who / which / where) | which
Correct it: The girl which won is Ana. | The girl who won is Ana.
Commas or not? 'My mum who is a nurse works nights.' (commas / no commas) | commas
She's the teacher ____ helped me most. (who / whose / which) | who
Valencia, ____ I was born, is on the coast. (which / where / that) | where

units.grammar: Present perfect and past simple. Present perfect (have/has + past participle) links past and present: for situations that started in the past and continue, and for past events when the time isn't given: I've lost my keys. Use it for things repeated in a period up to now: She's phoned three times this morning.
existing_questions_sample: I ____ (see) that film last week. | saw
____ (you / ever / try) Japanese food? | Have you ever tried
Correct it: I've finished my project yesterday. | I finished my project yesterday.
We haven't had lunch ____. (yet / already / just) | yet
She ____ (just / leave). You missed her by a minute. | has just left
My grandparents ____ (get) married in 1975. | got
I've ____ done my homework, so I can go out. (yet / already / still) | already
He ____ hasn't replied to my message. (yet / still / just) | still
Correct it: Did you ever be to London? | Have you ever been to London?
They ____ (live) here since 2015, and they love it. | have lived
When ____ (you / buy) those trainers? | did you buy
I ____ (never / ride) a horse in my life. | have never ridden

units.unit_title: Modals of ability and possibility and managed to
units.grammar: Modals of ability and possibility and managed to. Present ability: can / can't or am/is/are able to: I can swim but I can't dive. General ability in the past: could / couldn't or was/were able to: My gran could speak three languages. For success on one specific occasion in the past use managed to or was/were able to, NOT could: The door was stuck, but we managed to open it. (couldn't is fine in the negative.)
existing_questions_sample: When I was five, I ____ ride a bike. (could / managed / can) | could
The exam was hard, but I ____ to pass. (could / managed / can) | managed
Next year I'll ____ vote. (can / be able to / could) | be able to
Correct it: She will can come. | She will be able to come.
I haven't ____ to find my keys. (could / been able / can) | been able
We ____ not be able to come; I'll tell you later. (might / can / must) | might
It was foggy, so we ____ see anything. (couldn't / can't / managed) | couldn't
The fire spread fast, but everyone ____ able to escape. (was / did / could) | was
____ you swim when you were little? (Could / Can / Managed) | Could
After two hours he finally ____ fix it. (could / managed to / can) | managed to
She's very clever: she ____ speak four languages. (can / could / manages) | can
Did you ____ to get tickets in the end? (could / manage / able) | manage

units.grammar: Future (1): plans and intentions. Present simple for timetables and fixed schedules: The museum opens at ten tomorrow. School starts on 9 September. Present continuous for arrangements with a time or person already fixed: I'm seeing the dentist on Tuesday. be going to for intentions and plans you have already decided: I'm going to learn to drive this summer.
existing_questions_sample: The concert ____ (start) at 9 p.m. tomorrow. (timetable) | starts
'The phone's ringing.' 'OK, I ____ answer it.' ('ll / 'm going to / am) | 'll
We ____ (fly) to Rome on Friday; we've got the tickets. | are flying
I've decided: I ____ study medicine. (will / am going to / go) | am going to
Put in order: probably / I'll / late / be | I'll probably be late
Correct it: I won't probably come. | I probably won't come.
What time ____ your bus leave tomorrow? (does / will / is) | does
She ____ definitely going to pass. (will / is / does) | is
I promise I ____ (not / tell) anyone your secret. | won't tell
____ (you / do) anything on Saturday night? (arrangement) | Are you doing
Correct it: I'm going to definitely call you. | I'm definitely going to call you.
My cousin ____ (get) married in June; everything is booked. | is getting

units.grammar: Future (2): predictions. be going to for predictions based on evidence you can see or know now: Look at those clouds; it's going to rain. will for predictions based on opinion or belief, often with I think, I'm sure, probably: I think Brazil will win. Future continuous (will be + -ing) for an action in progress at a future time: This time next week I'll be lying on a beach.
existing_questions_sample: Watch out! That glass ____ fall. (will be / is going to / might be) | is going to
I'm sure you ____ love this book. (will / are going / may be) | will
This time tomorrow I ____ (sit) on the plane. | will be sitting
It ____ rain later; I'm not sure. (will / might / is going to) | might
Correct it: At six I will be work. | At six I will be working.
She hasn't studied at all. She ____ fail. (is going to / may not / will be) | is going to
We ____ not get tickets; they're selling fast. (may / will be / going to) | may
Do you think computers ____ replace teachers? (will / are / going) | will
Don't call at eight; we ____ (have) dinner then. | will be having
Which is less certain? (will / could) | could
In ten years' time I ____ (work) abroad, I hope. | will be working
He's driving too fast! He ____ crash! ('s going to / might not / 'll be) | 's going to

units.grammar: The passive. Form: the right tense of be + past participle: Coffee is grown in Brazil. The bridge was built in 1900. The hall is being cleaned. My bike has been stolen. Use the passive when we don't know or don't care who does the action, or when the action or object is more important. Add by + agent only when it is important to say who did it: This song was written by a teenager.
existing_questions_sample: English ____ (speak) all over the world. | is spoken
The Mona Lisa ____ (paint) by Leonardo da Vinci. | was painted
My bike ____ (steal)! I can't find it anywhere. (present perfect) | has been stolen
Helmets must ____ (wear) at all times. | be worn
Correct it: The house was build in 1950. | The house was built in 1950.
Make it passive: They clean the classrooms every day. The classrooms ____ every day. | are cleaned
The road ____ (repair) at the moment, so it's closed. | is being repaired
This book was written ____ a 15-year-old. (by / for / from) | by
The results ____ (announce) tomorrow. (will) | will be announced
Dinner ____ (not / serve) yet. (present perfect) | hasn't been served
Make it passive: Someone found my wallet. My wallet ____. | was found
This problem can ____ (solve) easily. | be solved

units.grammar: Present perfect continuous. Form: have/has been + -ing: I've been waiting. She hasn't been sleeping well. Have you been crying? Use it for an activity that started in the past and is still going on or has just stopped, often with a visible result: You're all wet! - I've been washing the car. Use it with for, since and how long to stress how long an activity has lasted: We've been playing for two hours.
existing_questions_sample: I ____ (wait) for you for an hour! | have been waiting
How long ____ (you / learn) English? | have you been learning
She ____ (read) three books this month. | has read
Correct it: I've been knowing him for years. | I've known him for years.
Your eyes are red. ____ you been crying? (Have / Did / Are) | Have
It ____ (rain) all day and it still hasn't stopped. | has been raining
We've been living here ____ March. (for / since) | since
He ____ (break) his leg, so he can't play. | has broken
I'm out of breath because I ____ (run). | have been running
They ____ (not / work) very hard lately. (continuous) | haven't been working
How many pages ____ (you / write) so far? | have you written
She's been studying ____ three hours. (for / since) | for

units.grammar: Zero and first conditionals. Zero conditional: if + present, present, for things that are always or generally true; here if means almost the same as when: If you heat ice, it melts. First conditional: if + present, will + infinitive, for a real possibility in the future and its result: If it rains, we'll stay in. Never use will in the if-clause: If I see her (NOT will see), I'll tell her.
existing_questions_sample: If you mix blue and yellow, you ____ (get) green. | get
If it ____ (snow) tomorrow, we'll make a snowman. | snows
I ____ (call) you if I miss the bus. | will call
Correct it: If it will rain, we'll stay. | If it rains, we'll stay.
Plants die if they ____ (not / get) water. | don't get
If you don't hurry, you ____ (miss) the train. | will miss
If we're lucky, we ____ see dolphins, but I'm not sure. (will / might / do) | might
____ I get home tonight, I'll text you. (it's certain) (If / When) | When
She ____ (not / pass) if she doesn't study. | won't pass
If you ____ (press) this button, the screen turns off. | press
What ____ (you / do) if the shop is closed? | will you do
Comma or not? 'I'll help you if I have time.' (comma / no comma) | no comma

units.grammar: Reported statements. When the reporting verb is past (said, told), the tense usually moves one step back: present -> past, past simple and present perfect -> past perfect: 'I'm tired' -> She said she was tired. will -> would, can -> could, may -> might, must -> had to, am going to -> was going to. could, would, should, might and the past perfect don't change.
existing_questions_sample: 'I like pizza.' -> He said he ____ pizza. | liked
'We are leaving.' -> They said they ____ leaving. | were
'I will help you.' -> She said she ____ help me. | would
'I can't swim.' -> He said he ____ swim. | couldn't
He ____ me that he was tired. (said / told) | told
'I saw Ana yesterday.' -> He said he had seen Ana ____. (the day before / the next day / that day) | the day before
'I've finished.' -> She said she ____ finished. | had
'We must go.' -> They said they ____ go. | had to
'I'll call you tomorrow.' -> She said she'd call me ____. (the day before / the next day / that day) | the next day
She ____ that she was busy. (said / told) | said
'I'm going to win.' -> He said he ____ going to win. | was
'I live here.' -> She said she lived ____. (here / there / that) | there

units.grammar: Reported questions; reported requests. Tenses, pronouns and time words change just as in reported statements: 'Where do you live?' -> He asked where I lived. Word order is like a statement (subject before verb) and there is no question mark: He asked where the bank was, NOT where was the bank. Don't use do, does or did in reported questions: 'Why did you leave?' -> She asked why I had left.
existing_questions_sample: 'Where do you live?' -> She asked me where I ____. | lived
'Are you hungry?' -> He asked ____ I was hungry. (if / that / what) | if
Correct it: She asked where was the station. | She asked where the station was.
'Can you help me?' -> He asked me ____ help him. (to / if / that) | to
'Please don't be late.' -> She asked us ____ late. | not to be
'How old is he?' -> She asked how old ____. | he was
'Did you see the match?' -> She asked if I ____ the match. | had seen
Correct it: He asked me what did I want. | He asked me what I wanted.
'Will you come?' -> They asked whether I ____ come. | would
'Open the window, please.' -> She asked me ____ the window. | to open
'Why are you crying?' -> He asked her why she ____. | was crying
'Have you finished?' -> The teacher asked if we ____. | had finished

units.unit_title: Have/get something done; get someone to do something
units.grammar: Have/get something done; get someone to do something. have/get + object + past participle = another person (usually a professional) does the job for you: I had my watch repaired. She's getting her nails done. get is more informal than have; both can be used in any tense: We're going to have the kitchen painted. Add by + person only if it matters who did it: I had my portrait painted by a street artist.
existing_questions_sample: I ____ my teeth checked yesterday. (had / did / made) | had
She's going to get her ears ____ (pierce). | pierced
We got the waiter ____ (take) a photo of us. | to take
Put in order: had / I / fixed / my phone | I had my phone fixed
He ____ his wallet stolen on the bus. (had / made / did) | had
My parents are having the house ____ (paint) this week. | painted
I'll get my dad ____ (drive) us to the station. | to drive
Who painted it? 'Eva had her room painted.' (Eva / someone else) | someone else
You should ____ your eyes tested. (get / make / do) | get
Correct it: I got Ana help me. | I got Ana to help me.
We ____ (have) our car washed every month. | have
Did you ____ your photo taken for the passport? (have / make / be) | have

units.grammar: Second conditional. Form: if + past simple, would + infinitive (or the other way round, without a comma): If I had more time, I'd learn Chinese. Use it for imaginary or unlikely situations in the present or future: If I won the lottery, I'd buy a boat. might instead of would makes the result less certain; could = would be able to: If you asked her, she might say yes.
existing_questions_sample: If I ____ (have) a car, I'd drive to school. | had
If she studied more, she ____ (pass) the exam. | would pass
If I ____ you, I'd apologise. (were / am / be) | were
Correct it: If I would have time, I'd help. | If I had time, I'd help.
I wish I ____ (know) the answer, but I don't. | knew
If only we ____ (not / have) an exam tomorrow! | didn't have
I wish you ____ stop making that noise! (would / will / did) | would
What ____ (you / do) if you found a wallet? | would you do
If we lived by the sea, we ____ go surfing, but I'm not sure. (might / will / can) | might
I wish I ____ play the piano. (could / can / would to) | could
He ____ (not / be) so tired if he went to bed earlier. | wouldn't be
Real or imaginary? 'If I had wings, I'd fly.' (real / imaginary) | imaginary

units.grammar: Modals of deduction: present. Use modal + infinitive to say how sure you are about a present situation. must = I'm almost sure it's true: She must be tired; she's been working all day. can't = I'm almost sure it's NOT true (don't use mustn't for this): That can't be Tom; he's in Paris. may, might, could = it's possible; add well (may well, might well) when it's quite probable: He might be at the gym. It may well rain.
existing_questions_sample: She's yawning. She ____ be tired. (must / can't / mustn't) | must
That ____ be Dan; Dan is much taller. (must / can't / might) | can't
I'm not sure where Eva is. She ____ be in the library. (might / must / can't) | might
Correct it: It mustn't be true! | It can't be true!
The lights are on, so someone ____ be at home. (must / can't / might not) | must
It's only a guess, but this ____ be the right street. (could / must / can't) | could
You've just had lunch! You ____ be hungry again! (can't / must / may) | can't
Don't phone now; they might ____ (have) dinner. | be having
He ____ not know the answer; ask someone else. (might / must / could) | might
How sure? 'It must be broken.' (almost sure / just possible) | almost sure
Her French is perfect. She ____ have French parents. (may well / can't / mustn't) | may well
Which means 'perhaps not'? (might not / can't) | might not

units.grammar: Third conditional. Form: if + past perfect, would have + past participle: If I'd seen you, I would have said hello. Use it for imaginary situations in the past (things that did not happen) and their imagined results: If we'd left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train. (We left late and missed it.) might have = the result was only possible; could have = would have been able to: If you'd asked, I might have helped.
existing_questions_sample: If I ____ (know) about the party, I'd have gone. | had known
If she had run faster, she ____ (win) the race. | would have won
If I ____ seen him, I'd have waved. (had / would have / have) | had
I wish I ____ (not / eat) so much cake last night. | hadn't eaten
We ____ (not / get) lost if we'd taken a map. | wouldn't have got
If only I ____ (bring) my umbrella this morning! | had brought
'If it had rained, we'd have stayed home.' Did it rain? (yes / no) | no
If you'd told me, I ____ have helped, but I'm not certain. (might / will / can) | might
In 'If I'd known', 'd = ____. (had / would) | had
In 'I'd have called', 'd = ____. (had / would) | would
What ____ (you / do) if you had missed the flight? | would you have done
She wishes she ____ (study) harder for last week's test. | had studied

units.grammar: Modals of deduction: past. Use modal + have + past participle to make guesses about the past. must have = I'm almost sure it happened: The grass is wet; it must have rained. can't have / couldn't have = I'm almost sure it didn't happen: She can't have left; her coat is still here. may have, might have, could have = perhaps it happened: He might have missed the bus.
existing_questions_sample: The street is wet. It ____ have rained. (must / can't / might not) | must
He ____ have stolen it; he was with me all day. (can't / must / may) | can't
I'm not sure why she's late. She ____ have missed the bus. (might / must / can't) | might
Correct it: She must has forgotten. | She must have forgotten.
They must have ____ (go) out; nobody's answering. | gone
You ____ have seen Leo in town; he's in Peru! (can't / must / might) | can't
He didn't reply. He ____ not have seen my text. (might / must / can) | might
She got 10 in the exam. She ____ have studied a lot. (must / can't / might not) | must
Where are my keys? I could have ____ (leave) them at school. | left
How sure? 'He may have called.' (almost sure / just possible) | just possible
Correct it: They can't had finished already. | They can't have finished already.
The window is broken. Someone ____ (must / break) it. | must have broken

units.grammar: -ing forms. The -ing form can be the subject or object of a sentence: Swimming is great exercise. I've finished tidying my room. Use -ing after verbs of liking and disliking (love, enjoy, hate, can't stand, don't mind): I can't stand queuing. Always use -ing after a preposition, including adjective + preposition: She's good at drawing. I'm tired of waiting. He left without saying goodbye.
existing_questions_sample: ____ (eat) too much sugar is bad for you. | Eating
I'm interested in ____ (learn) Japanese. | learning
She's really good at ____ (dance). | dancing
Correct it: He left without to say goodbye. | He left without saying goodbye.
Do you enjoy ____ (play) board games? | playing
____ (not / want) to be late, I took a taxi. | Not wanting
____ (feel) hungry, we stopped for a sandwich. | Feeling
I saw a man ____ (climb) through the window. | climbing
Correct it: I'm afraid of fly. | I'm afraid of flying.
Who was walking? 'Walking to school, Ana found a coin.' (Ana / the coin) | Ana
Thank you for ____ (help) me with my project. | helping
I don't mind ____ (wait) a few minutes. | waiting
